Theme 078 · Characters & mascots

Rubber-Hose Gloves

A 1930s-cartoon world on cream film stock: noodle arms, four-finger white gloves, pie-cut eyes and iris transitions. Pulse is a teal alarm clock with legs — it watches the hours, and when checkout breaks it rings its bells and points; a human hand pushes the plunger.

readability ●●○trust ●●○effort high
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Gloved hands juggle dashboard frames in a loop that speeds up each bar; the title card holds still (with film weave) and a frame drops on the 0:06 snare.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

The iris opens on the drop (circle wipe, 0.3 s power2.out) onto the clock character springing up, arms out; the sunburst rotates slowly and the ribbon unfurls left-to-right over beat 2.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

The bells shake on every 16th as the alarm rings; the gloved finger jabs at the chalkboard on beat 1, the −18% writes itself in chalk over 2 beats, and the human hand presses ROLL BACK on the next downbeat — the plunger drops.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The iris closes to a circle around the tagline on beat 1, the clock waves from the corner in rubber-hose loops (2 frames per 8th), and Start free stamps in on the final hit.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Alarm-clock mascot — Pulse: teal clock with bells, pie-cut eyes and a coral hammer knob
  • Rubber-hose limbs — jointless black noodle arms/legs ending in four-finger white gloves
  • Title card — double-ruled frame with corner studs for hook lines
  • Iris wipe — circular black matte that opens and closes scenes
  • Chalkboard — framed board for the anomaly readout
  • Plunger box — wooden detonator-style ROLL BACK pressed by a real (ungloved) hand

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Rubber-hose cycle — limbs loop in 4-drawing cycles on 2s (12 fps), one cycle per beat at 120 BPM — the classic bounce-to-the-music feel
  • Iris in/out — circle radius 0↔430 px in 0.3 s power2.out, opening exactly on the drop and closing on the final bar
  • Ring shake — bells jitter ±10 px on 16th notes with 3-frame holds; motion lines flash on the offbeats

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: Old-cartoon rhythm is literally built on music (bounce-to-the-beat), so it cuts to a 120 BPM track naturally; an alarm clock is a perfect metaphor for an agent that watches the time and rings when something happens. Risk: Heavy retro stylisation can feel like a parody and the look is expensive to animate well; keep data on the chalkboard in clean modern type so the proof stays credible.

Adapt to your product: Pick an everyday object that matches your product’s job (clock, mailbox, safe, thermometer) and give it gloves and pie-eyes; your real numbers go on a chalkboard or title card.
